messages.body_plain:
Hi Renaud,

I thought I'd send these notes on the chance that they'd be helpful to others. I installed NMF, but have not yet run it. The one thing that was a bit odd is the warning (...is not available (for R version 3.0.0)).

I've been using v0.9 for some time on R v2.15.x, on OS X 10.7.5. Today I updated R to v3.0.0, and got an error message when installing from the v0.9 .tgz from the latest RStudio (which is how I'd installed NMF on v2.15.x).

RStudio did not recognize that v0.16.2 was available at CRAN (seeing only NMFN available, but not NMF), and after trying to install a few .tar.gz versions from your CRAN-like web page (but failing to achieve a loadable library), a Google search suggested I look at CRAN. From there I downloaded v0.16.2's tar.gz, and installed it from RStudio's GUI installer.  All seemed OK.

Renaud,

With R 3.0.0, I get an error when I try to run a test. I'm likely missing something simple. Could you help me resolve this?

messages.subject: [NMF-user] [ANN] NMF 0.16.2 released on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Dear NMF enthusiasts,

the NMF package is finally back on CRAN (version 0.16.2), and should
install on all platform using:

install.packages('NMF')

from you preferred CRAN mirror. Spread the word!

Builds on R-forge are still broken for some packages, including NMF
unfortunately. So until this gets fixed, development versions will be
hosted on myCRAN repository at:

http://web.cbio.uct.ac.za/~renaud/CRAN

An issue with the shared memory feature for parallel computations on Mac
have already been reported. I will need to investigate this further. For
now, try disabling the shared memory feature:

nmf.options(shared.memory=FALSE)

IMPORTANT: please note that R-3.0.0 has just been released and that CRAN
ask users to reinstall all previously installed packages for everything
(not just NMF) to work properly.

I hope this release facilitates your work and research using NMF
methodologies.
As usual, questions/bugs/feature requests are welcome and should be sent to
this list, so that everybody benefit from them.

Bests,
Renaud


-- 

Renaud Gaujoux
Computational Biology - University of Cape Town
South Africa

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I saw this error on CRAN's Mac check logs as well. This seems to be linked
with the shared.memory feature when running parallel computations, on Mac
only.
I have no Mac to thoroughly check and asked the author of bigmemory to see
if he could reproduce the error: he could not when running the example in
an R console, but got an error when running the checks.
So this will need further investigations.

Did you reinstall all packages, specially bigmemory, after upgrading to
R-3.0.0?

You should still be able to run parallel computations but disabling
shared.memory by:

nmf.options(shared.memory=FALSE)

If you do not want to remember/type this every time you load NMF, you could
simply uninstall the synchronicity package, which you probably do not need
otherwise. The shared memory feature will then be disabled for good.

Bests,
Renaud

Hi,

I saw this error on CRAN's Mac check logs as well. This seems to be linked with the shared.memory feature when running parallel computations, on Mac only.
I have no Mac to thoroughly check and asked the author of bigmemory to see if he could reproduce the error: he could not when running the example in an R console, but got an error when running the checks.
So this will need further investigations.

Did you reinstall all packages, specially bigmemory, after upgrading to R-3.0.0?

You should still be able to run parallel computations but disabling shared.memory by:

nmf.options(shared.memory=FALSE)

If you do not want to remember/type this every time you load NMF, you could simply uninstall the synchronicity package, which you probably do not need otherwise. The shared memory feature will then be disabled for good.
